flags.description: Compares the total number of customer rows between model and reference.
flags.sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS DOUBLE) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS DOUBLE) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

flags.description: Compares the grand total of lifetime_revenue across all customers.
flags.sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

flags.description: Compares the grand total of lifetime_orders across all customers.
flags.sql: SELECT 'total' AS slice, (SELECT CAST(SUM(lifetime_orders) AS DOUBLE) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT CAST(SUM(lifetime_orders) AS DOUBLE) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

flags.description: Compares the revenue-weighted average order value (sum revenue / sum orders) overall, which exposes fan-out or exclusion bugs that per-row averages hide.

flags.sql: SELECT 'total_simple_mean_avg_order_supply_cost' AS slice, (SELECT AVG(avg_order_supply_cost) FROM model_output) AS model_value, (SELECT AVG(avg_order_supply_cost) FROM reference_output) AS reference_value

flags.description: Compares the count of customers with a NULL avg_order_value, which should be zero on both sides given the grain.
flags.sql: SELECT 'null_avg_order_value_count' AS slice, (SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS DOUBLE) FROM model_output WHERE avg_order_value IS NULL) AS model_value, (SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS DOUBLE) FROM reference_output WHERE avg_order_value IS NULL) AS reference_value

flags.description: Compares counts of customer_id keys present only in model, only in reference, and in both, to surface missing or extra qualifying customers.
flags.sql: WITH full_join AS (SELECT m.customer_id AS m_id, r.customer_id AS r_id FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id) SELECT 'only_in_model' AS slice, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN r_id IS NULL AND m_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) AS model_value, 0.0 AS reference_value FROM full_join UNION ALL SELECT 'only_in_reference' AS slice, 0.0 AS model_value, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN m_id IS NULL AND r_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) AS reference_value FROM full_join UNION ALL SELECT 'matched' AS slice, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN m_id IS NOT NULL AND r_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) AS model_value, CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN m_id IS NOT NULL AND r_id IS NOT NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) AS reference_value FROM full_join

flags.sql: SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, m.lifetime_revenue AS model_value, r.lifetime_revenue AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id

flags.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM first_order_date) AS VARCHAR) AS yr, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS rev FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT CAST(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM first_order_date) AS VARCHAR) AS yr, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS rev FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.yr, r.yr) AS slice, m.rev AS model_value, r.rev AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.yr = r.yr ORDER BY 1

flags.description: Compares customer counts bucketed by the calendar month of first_order_date.
flags.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT strftime(first_order_date,'%Y-%m') AS ym, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT strftime(first_order_date,'%Y-%m') AS ym, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.ym, r.ym) AS slice, CAST(m.cnt AS DOUBLE) AS model_value, CAST(r.cnt AS DOUBLE) AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.ym = r.ym ORDER BY 1

flags.sql: WITH r_min AS (SELECT MIN(strftime(first_order_date,'%Y-%m')) AS ym FROM reference_output) SELECT 'first_month_revenue' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM model_output WHERE strftime(first_order_date,'%Y-%m') = (SELECT ym FROM r_min)) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM reference_output WHERE strftime(first_order_date,'%Y-%m') = (SELECT ym FROM r_min)) AS reference_value

flags.description: Compares lifetime_revenue for the latest calendar month of first_order_date (per reference), a boundary-period edge case.
flags.sql: WITH r_max AS (SELECT MAX(strftime(first_order_date,'%Y-%m')) AS ym FROM reference_output) SELECT 'last_month_revenue' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM model_output WHERE strftime(first_order_date,'%Y-%m') = (SELECT ym FROM r_max)) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM reference_output WHERE strftime(first_order_date,'%Y-%m') = (SELECT ym FROM r_max)) AS reference_value

flags.description: Compares lifetime_revenue totals bucketed by lifetime_orders size (1, 2-5, 6-10, 11+), sensitive to order-count-dependent fan-out bugs.
flags.sql: WITH m AS (SELECT CASE WHEN lifetime_orders = 1 THEN '1' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 2 AND 5 THEN '2-5' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 6 AND 10 THEN '6-10' ELSE '11+' END AS bucket, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS rev FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT CASE WHEN lifetime_orders = 1 THEN '1' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 2 AND 5 THEN '2-5' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 6 AND 10 THEN '6-10' ELSE '11+' END AS bucket, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS rev FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.bucket, r.bucket) AS slice, m.rev AS model_value, r.rev AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.bucket = r.bucket ORDER BY 1

flags.sql: SELECT 'single_order_customers_count' AS slice, (SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS DOUBLE) FROM model_output WHERE lifetime_orders = 1) AS model_value, (SELECT CAST(COUNT(*) AS DOUBLE) FROM reference_output WHERE lifetime_orders = 1) AS reference_value

flags.sql: WITH top20 AS (SELECT customer_id FROM reference_output ORDER BY lifetime_revenue DESC LIMIT 20) SELECT COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) AS slice, m.avg_order_value AS model_value, r.avg_order_value AS reference_value FROM model_output m FULL OUTER JOIN reference_output r ON m.customer_id = r.customer_id WHERE COALESCE(m.customer_id, r.customer_id) IN (SELECT customer_id FROM top20)

ai.prompt:
A dbt model has been changed and must be reconciled against an independent reference dashboard before it ships.

## Model: customer_lifetime_value

### Business definition (from the model's YAML)
Lifetime value per customer. One row per real customer with at least one qualifying order (internal "QA Test Account" customers and refunded orders are excluded). lifetime_revenue is the sum of qualifying order totals including tax. avg_order_value is lifetime_revenue / lifetime_orders. avg_order_supply_cost is the mean supply cost over qualifying orders that have item records; orders with no item records are excluded from the average rather than counted as zero.

### Model SQL (dbt/Jinja, DuckDB dialect)
```sql
with

orders as (

    select * from {{ ref('orders') }}

),

customers as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_customers') }}

),

refunds as (

    select * from {{ ref('stg_refunds') }}

),

qualifying_orders as (

    select
        orders.*,
        customers.customer_name

    from orders

    inner join customers
        on orders.customer_id = customers.customer_id

    left join refunds
        on orders.order_id = refunds.order_id

    where not customers.is_test_account
        and refunds.order_id is null

)

select
    qualifying_orders.customer_id,
    qualifying_orders.customer_name,
    cast(min(qualifying_orders.ordered_at_ts) as date) as first_order_date,
    cast(max(qualifying_orders.ordered_at_ts) as date) as last_order_date,
    cast(count(qualifying_orders.order_id) as bigint) as lifetime_orders,
    cast(sum(qualifying_orders.order_total) as decimal(18, 2)) as lifetime_revenue,
    cast(sum(qualifying_orders.order_total) as double)
        / count(qualifying_orders.order_id) as avg_order_value,
    cast(avg(qualifying_orders.order_cost) as double) as avg_order_supply_cost

from qualifying_orders

inner join {{ ref('order_items') }} as order_items
    on qualifying_orders.order_id = order_items.order_id

group by 1, 2
```

## Tables available to your queries
Your queries run in a sandbox that contains exactly two tables and nothing else:

`model_output`: the model's output.
  - customer_id: VARCHAR
  - customer_name: VARCHAR
  - first_order_date: DATE
  - last_order_date: DATE
  - lifetime_orders: BIGINT
  - lifetime_revenue: DECIMAL(18,2)
  - avg_order_value: DOUBLE
  - avg_order_supply_cost: DOUBLE

`reference_output`: the trusted reference dashboard, computed independently from raw data at the same grain.
  - customer_id: VARCHAR
  - customer_name: VARCHAR
  - first_order_date: DATE
  - last_order_date: DATE
  - lifetime_orders: BIGINT
  - lifetime_revenue: DOUBLE
  - avg_order_value: DOUBLE
  - avg_order_supply_cost: DOUBLE

Grain (one row per): customer_id

## Task
Write up to 40 reconciliation queries comparing `model_output` to `reference_output`. Choose slices that would expose wrong numbers that still pass schema checks and data tests, for example: grand totals of each measure; totals by each dimension and dimension member; each available time grain (day, week, month, as applicable); edge periods (first/last periods, period boundaries); row counts and key coverage (keys present in one table but not the other); and averages/ratios where nulls or join fan-out could distort them.

Each query MUST return exactly these columns:
- `slice` (varchar): a human-readable label for the row, e.g. 'total', '2025-03 | Brooklyn'
- `model_value` (numeric): the value computed from model_output
- `reference_value` (numeric): the same value computed from reference_output

A query may return one row (a total) or many rows (one per slice). Use a full outer join on the slice keys so that slices missing on either side appear, with NULL on the missing side. Do not compute differences yourself; the harness compares model_value to reference_value. Return at most 5000 rows per query.

{"id": "month_first_order_revenue", "kind": "time_grain", "measure": "lifetime_revenue", "dimensions": ["first_order_date"], "time_grain": "month", "description": "Compares lifetime_revenue totals bucketed by the calendar month of first_order_date.", "sql": "WITH m AS (SELECT strftime(first_order_date, '%Y-%m') AS ym, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS rev FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT strftime(first_order_date, '%Y-%m') AS ym, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS rev FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.ym, r.ym) AS slice, m.rev AS model_value, r.rev AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.ym = r.ym ORDER BY 1"},
{"id": "month_last_order_orders", "kind": "time_grain", "measure": "lifetime_orders", "dimensions": ["last_order_date"], "time_grain": "month", "description": "Compares lifetime_orders totals bucketed by the calendar month of last_order_date.", "sql": "WITH m AS (SELECT strftime(last_order_date, '%Y-%m') AS ym, SUM(lifetime_orders) AS cnt FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT strftime(last_order_date, '%Y-%m') AS ym, SUM(lifetime_orders) AS cnt FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.ym, r.ym) AS slice, CAST(m.cnt AS DOUBLE) AS model_value, CAST(r.cnt AS DOUBLE) AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.ym = r.ym ORDER BY 1"},

{"id": "first_month_revenue", "kind": "edge", "measure": "lifetime_revenue", "dimensions": ["first_order_date"], "time_grain": "month", "description": "Compares lifetime_revenue for the earliest calendar month of first_order_date (per reference), a boundary-period edge case.", "sql": "WITH r_min AS (SELECT MIN(strftime(first_order_date,'%Y-%m')) AS ym FROM reference_output) SELECT 'first_month_revenue' AS slice, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM model_output WHERE strftime(first_order_date,'%Y-%m') = (SELECT ym FROM r_min)) AS model_value, (SELECT SUM(lifetime_revenue) FROM reference_output WHERE strftime(first_order_date,'%Y-%m') = (SELECT ym FROM r_min)) AS reference_value"},

{"id": "bucket_lifetime_orders_revenue", "kind": "dimension", "measure": "lifetime_revenue", "dimensions": ["lifetime_orders"], "time_grain": "none", "description": "Compares lifetime_revenue totals bucketed by lifetime_orders size (1, 2-5, 6-10, 11+), sensitive to order-count-dependent fan-out bugs.", "sql": "WITH m AS (SELECT CASE WHEN lifetime_orders = 1 THEN '1' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 2 AND 5 THEN '2-5' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 6 AND 10 THEN '6-10' ELSE '11+' END AS bucket, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS rev FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT CASE WHEN lifetime_orders = 1 THEN '1' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 2 AND 5 THEN '2-5' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 6 AND 10 THEN '6-10' ELSE '11+' END AS bucket, SUM(lifetime_revenue) AS rev FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.bucket, r.bucket) AS slice, m.rev AS model_value, r.rev AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.bucket = r.bucket ORDER BY 1"},

{"id": "bucket_lifetime_orders_avg_supply_cost", "kind": "dimension", "measure": "avg_order_supply_cost", "dimensions": ["lifetime_orders"], "time_grain": "none", "description": "Compares the simple mean of avg_order_supply_cost bucketed by lifetime_orders size, sensitive to item-join fan-out that scales with order count.", "sql": "WITH m AS (SELECT CASE WHEN lifetime_orders = 1 THEN '1' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 2 AND 5 THEN '2-5' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 6 AND 10 THEN '6-10' ELSE '11+' END AS bucket, AVG(avg_order_supply_cost) AS val FROM model_output GROUP BY 1), r AS (SELECT CASE WHEN lifetime_orders = 1 THEN '1' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 2 AND 5 THEN '2-5' WHEN lifetime_orders BETWEEN 6 AND 10 THEN '6-10' ELSE '11+' END AS bucket, AVG(avg_order_supply_cost) AS val FROM reference_output GROUP BY 1) SELECT COALESCE(m.bucket, r.bucket) AS slice, m.val AS model_value, r.val AS reference_value FROM m FULL OUTER JOIN r ON m.bucket = r.bucket ORDER BY 1"},
